study_type.claude: Experiment (preregistered two-phase controlled experiment; Phase 2 RCT)
study_type.nlm: Experiment (preregistered two-phase controlled experiment; Phase 2 RCT)

research_method.claude: Preregistered two-phase controlled experiment: Phase 1 feature implementation with/without AI (observational), Phase 2 RCT in which new developers evolve the code without AI (40 treatment, 35 control); frequentist and Bayesian causal analysis; qualitative free-text analysis; static analysis with CodeScene, PMD, RefactoringMiner
research_method.nlm: Preregistered two-phase controlled experiment with Phase 2 RCT; 151 valid participants (76 Phase 1, 75 Phase 2); frequentist tests and Bayesian analysis; CodeScene, PMD, JaCoCo in CI
research_method.value: Preregistered two-phase controlled experiment: Phase 1 participants add a feature to a Java/Spring Boot app with or without AI assistance (observational, 76 solutions); Phase 2 RCT in which 75 new participants evolve those solutions without AI; outcomes completion time, CodeHealth, test coverage, perceived productivity; frequentist tests (Wilcoxon, Cliff's delta) plus Bayesian causal analysis, static analysis (CodeScene, PMD) and qualitative coding of free-text answers
research_method.note: Phase 2 split (40 treatment, 35 control) and RefactoringMiner reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry/mixed; volunteers from many organizations and countries (95% professionals), Java/Spring Boot RecipeFinder system (2 KLoC); 449 pre-screened, 151 valid participants
context.nlm: Industry/mixed; professional developers from various international organizations and the Equal Experts community; 449 sign-ups, 151 valid participants (76 Phase 1, 75 Phase 2)
context.value: industry; volunteer developers from many organizations and countries (about 95% professionals), small Java/Spring Boot web app (RecipeFinder, ~2 KLoC); 449 pre-screened, 151 participants with valid tasks (76 in Phase 1, 75 in Phase 2)
context.note: Both label the setting 'Industry / Mixed' (cross-organization volunteer sample).

dora_applied.note: NotebookLM: DORA only referenced in background; Claude: not reported.

space_applied.note: SPACE frames productivity and structures the 10-item perceived productivity Likert scale (S, C, E items).

ai_discussed.note: AI assistant use is the independent variable.

remote_covid.note: Both give work mode 'Remote' only because participants completed tasks remotely in their own environment; remote work is not a topic of the study.

data_window.note: Claude: study conducted in late 2024; NotebookLM states no period (only that it predates third-generation agents).

cat_quality.note: CodeHealth, test coverage (JaCoCo), code smells and PMD violations.

cat_collaboration.note: SPACE 'C' items concern information seeking; team dynamics explicitly out of scope.

cat_satisfaction.note: Satisfaction (S) items in the perceived productivity scale (fulfilled, frustrated).

cat_activity.note: Git activity (commits, added/deleted lines, changed files) reported descriptively.

cat_devex.note: Both label perceived productivity partly 'DevEx', but the DevEx framework is not used.

cat_survey.note: Pre-screening and exit questionnaires (5-point Likert perceived productivity scale, Cronbach's alpha 0.82).

evidence.quote: We conducted a two-phase, preregistered controlled experiment involving 151 participants, 95% of whom were professional developers.

In Phase 1, participants added a new feature to a Java web application, with or without AI assistance. In Phase 2, a randomized controlled trial, new participants evolved these solutions without AI assistance.
Perceived Productivity (PP) is a subjective assessment based on the SPACE framework (see Section 2.1). We measured PP using a Likert scale
we consider the time it takes to implement changes a valid proxy for maintainability.
CodeHealth (CH) was measured as a project-level weighted average over all files in the codebase, i.e., not only the files modified by the participant.
the resulting coverage was measured using the Java code coverage library JaCoCo, integrated into the continuous integration pipeline via the same GitHub Action.
